conviction_note: Abs move 13% (implied 11.4%, own median 13.1%, raised for a multi-year investor-day reset landing at 08:00 ET inside the window) times a slight lean up (p_up 54). The lean comes from Celestica's record of beating the top of its own guide, TSMC saying on 2026-10-15 that AI demand still exceeds supply, and a July-like setup (24% fall in 20 days with no company-specific cause, short interest only 3.9%). It is held near 50 by a +8.3 put skew, by this name selling beat-and-raises twice in 2026 (-13.1%, -14.4%), and by a Q3 EPS consensus that may not reflect the August dilution. The findings sum to +1.2, close to the scaled +1.04, because nothing decides the sign.
bar: Q3 revenue: company guide $5.25-5.55bn (midpoint $5.40bn) per the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001030894/000103089426000043/cls-20260630prcondensedfs.htm, 2026-07-27). Estimate sources agree within about 2%: MarketBeat $5.37bn, Investing.com $5.44bn (https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/will-celesticas-q3-results-live-up-to-lofty-market-expectations-93CH-4972772, 2026-10-26), Benzinga $5.47bn, Zacks $5.4bn. Adj EPS: guide $2.88-3.08, set BEFORE the August 9.68M-share raise. Consensus is $2.94-3.01, but Bernstein has $2.79 and says consensus misses the dilution (https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/bernstein-reiterates-celestica-stock-rating-ahead-of-earnings-93CH-4912491, about 2026-10-15), so the EPS bar is disputed. FY2026 outlook: $20.5bn revenue, $11.30 adj EPS (assumes no new shares). 2027: the company says growth will accelerate beyond 65% (a floor of about $33.8bn); Bernstein models $40bn revenue and $24.19 EPS and says buy-side expectations are aligned with that. print_vs_bar_pct is measured against $5.44bn revenue.
positioning_check: Short interest 4,437,263 shares, 3.9% of float, 1.95-2.0 days to cover as of 2026-09-30, up 14.9% from 09-15 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/CLS/short-interest/ and https://equibles.com/stocks/cls/shortinterest; FINRA published 2026-10-09). Not a crowded short, so a squeeze is a weak mechanism. Skew_25d is +8.26 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 1.34, ATM IV 136%, event-implied move 11.37%. Tape: -24.2% over 20 days, -10.0% over 5 days, -42.8% from the 52-week high, 8.3% above the 52-week low. Sell-side is near-unanimous Buy (24 of 25 per MarketBeat 2026-10-24), with a mean target about $448 against a spot of about $270. Insiders have sold continuously under 10b5-1 plans (CEO about $130.7M over six months).

findings.finding: Celestica has repeatedly reported above the top of its own guide: Q2 2026 revenue was $4.70bn against a $4.15-4.45bn guide (5.6% over the top) and adj EPS $2.54 against $2.14-2.34, and it has beaten consensus EPS 8 quarters running. TSMC, a direct upstream counterparty, reported on 2026-10-15 that Q3 revenue was $46.7bn, above its own $44.6-45.8bn guide, and said AI demand 'still exceeds supply'. A Q3 revenue print of about $5.6bn (+3% against the $5.44bn consensus, at or just over the $5.55bn top of the guide) is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name sells beats. Q1 2026 beat and raised, then -14.4% (2026-04-27; it had run up 60% into the print). Q4 2025 printed -13.1% (2026-01-28). Q2 2026 beat by 5.6% over the guide top, raised the year and promised faster 2027 growth, and rose +10.0% (2026-07-27), coming from 31% off the high.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue ($5.37-5.47bn) sits at the guide midpoint, not at the top where the company has recently landed. If the market expected a repeat of Q2's 5% beat over the guide top, consensus would sit near $5.8bn. However, a beat of this kind is the expected pattern and is largely in the price, so the finding is small.
findings.independence: TSMC Q3 beat its own guide and said demand exceeds supply (https://www.crnasia.com/news/2026/components-and-peripherals/tsmc-third-quarter-revenue-tops-guidance-as-ceo-says-ai-dema, 2026-10-15). Jabil's FQ4 to Aug 31 beat revenue at $10.6bn against $9.69bn on AI demand (https://finviz.com/news/397095/jabil-shares-fall-4-despite-fourth-quarter-earnings-beat-and-higher-fiscal-2027-outlook, 2026-09-30).

findings.finding: Q3 adj EPS guidance ($2.88-3.08) was set on 2026-07-27, before the $3bn raise of 9,677,419 shares at $310 closed on about 2026-08-07/12. That adds about 8.4% to the share count, or about 5% weighted over Q3. Bernstein models $2.79 against a $2.94-3.01 consensus and says some estimates omit the dilution. A headline EPS that looks in line, or short of a stale $2.97, is plausible even if operations beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Celestica print carried a dilution mismatch. The stock fell about 13% on the raise itself (Aug 2026), so this line has moved the stock before.
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregator consensus ($2.94-3.01) still sits at or above the pre-dilution guide midpoint of $2.98. If the dilution were in the bar, the published consensus would sit near $2.80-2.85. The effect is mechanical and the operating beat may offset it, so the size is small.
findings.independence: The completed offering is confirmed at 9,677,419 shares at $310 (https://corporate.celestica.com/node/17646, 2026-08-05; completion per the company 2026-08-12). A separate source says the FY $11.30 guide assumes no new shares and that dilution cuts 2026 EPS by 3.3-3.7% (https://kalkine.com/news/technology/investors-weigh-celesticas-3b-raise-against-eps-headwinds).

findings.finding: The 2026-10-27 08:00 ET call is also Celestica's 2026 Investor and Analyst Day, so multi-year targets land inside the window. The company has already said 2027 revenue growth will exceed 65% (a floor of about $33.8bn on $20.5bn) with EPS growing faster. It is spending a $1.5bn capex placeholder for 2027, funded partly by the $3bn August raise, which is what the money buys. Bernstein models 2027 revenue at $40bn and EPS at $24.19, says the buy-side is aligned, and puts 2028 EPS at $36 against a sell-side $27. The stock has fallen about 16% since that note, so the priced 2027 bar is likely below $40bn and a target at or above it would land as a beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guidance line has decided this stock. Q2 2026 brought a raise plus 2027 acceleration: +10.0%. Q1 2026 brought a raise that fell short of lofty expectations: -14.4%. Investing.com (2026-10-26) says a solid beat may not spark a rally unless guidance is raised.
findings.why_not_priced: The event is known, but its content is not. Spot about $270 against a mean sell-side target of about $448, and a 24% fall in 20 days, show the market has marked down the 2027-28 path that Bernstein says the buy-side held at $40bn on 2026-10-15. If $40bn+ were still priced, the stock would sit near its mid-October $320s. The financing question has an answer: the money funds capacity for a ramp the company has already guided to, so it supports the target and is not a negative.
findings.independence: Q2 release statement on 2027 >65% growth and EPS growing faster than revenue (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001030894/000103089426000043/cls-20260630prcondensedfs.htm). Bernstein's 2027 $40.03bn and its sum of Jalapeno, TPU-rack and 1.6T-switch upside (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/celestica-aktie-bernstein-bestatigt-outperform-mit-520-dollar-kursziel). Shares the Bernstein document with finding 2, but a different line.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print matches the July setup that was bought, not the April setup that was sold. CLS is -24.2% over 20 days and -42.8% from its 52-week high. Three October articles attribute the fall to a sector-wide AI derating (OpenAI revenue report 10-08, Broadcom CEO's 'casino' remark 10-12, hot CPI 10-14, Anthropic's slower Q3 growth about 10-15), not to any company announcement. Short interest is low (3.9%, 2 days) and the Street is 24 of 25 Buy. In April the stock ran up 60% into the print and fell 14.4%; in July it came in 31% off the high and rose 10.0%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-04-27: +60% run-in, -14.4%. 2026-07-27: 31% off the high, +10.0%. Two observations, so the relation is a lean, not a rule.
findings.why_not_priced: The +8.26 put skew says the options market expects more downside. The argument that it is wrong about this print: the skew follows a 24% sector-driven drawdown and 66% realised vol, while the company-level inputs (guide-beat record, TSMC demand, an already-promised 2027 acceleration) are unchanged since July. This is a sign against the skew, so the size is kept small.
findings.independence: Investing.com 2026-10-16 likewise finds no 'single new negative development' (https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-celestica-stock-sliding-today-93CH-4954516). The short-interest level is from MarketBeat and Equibles (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/CLS/short-interest/).

findings.finding: Meta, a hyperscaler customer of Celestica, reported Q3 on 2026-10-21, after Celestica last spoke. Revenue was $64.6bn against $63.3bn expected, and it narrowed 2026 capex to $135-145bn from $130-145bn (low end raised) but gave no 2027 capex outlook. CLS then fell 9.8% on 10-22, so the market read the missing 2027 number as a negative while the 2026 spend firmed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean measurement exists. CLS fell 9.8% the day after Meta's print, which suggests the hyperscaler capex line already moves this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced, in the 10-22 fall. The small residual is that a firmer 2026 Meta spend supports Celestica's Q4 implied guide of about $6.35bn ($20.5bn less Q1 $4.05bn, Q2 $4.70bn and Q3 about $5.40bn), which a fall read off the 2027 silence does not reflect. The finding is a proxy, so its size is small.
findings.independence: Fortune on Meta capex and settlements (https://fortune.com/2026/10/21/meta-q3-earnings-mark-zuckerberg-capex-muse/, 2026-10-21). Alphabet, the TPU customer, reports 2026-10-28, which is outside the window.

findings.finding: Sector demand-quality doubts in October are proxies that could temper the tone of the investor-day targets. Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said on 2026-10-12 that access to capital may become the main limit on AI build speed, which bears on Celestica's customers. The FT reported Anthropic's Q3 revenue at $16.8bn, with sequential growth slowing to about 50% from about 145%; Anthropic is a major TPU user.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In April 2026 a raise that fell short of AI-level expectations sold off 14.4%, so the guidance-tone line is the one that has punished this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: these are the stated causes of the 24% fall. A residual remains only if management hedges its 2027 targets on customer financing. This is macro-to-company transmission no Celestica document confirms, so the size is small.
findings.independence: Anthropic's slower Q3 growth and the chip sell-off (https://moneycheck.com/?p=187675); TSMC also called 2027 more cautious on macro (https://www.crnasia.com/news/2026/components-and-peripherals/tsmc-third-quarter-revenue-tops-guidance-as-ceo-says-ai-dema). Both cut against TSMC's 'demand exceeds supply' in finding 1.

findings.finding: Peer reaction function: Jabil (2026-09-30) beat FQ4 revenue ($10.6bn against $9.69bn) and EPS ($4.40 against $4.06), and guided FY27 above consensus ($44.5bn against $42.9bn; EPS $17.55 against $16.92). Its shares still fell about 4% pre-market. AI-EMS beat-and-raise prints are currently being sold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the peer's own line. Celestica sold off after beat-and-raises in January and April 2026 and was bought in July.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a reaction-function datum, not a fact about Celestica's number. It is filed small because it argues against reading a beat as a rise.
findings.independence: Parameter.io on the same Jabil reaction (https://parameter.io/jabil-jbl-stock-drops-3-after-strong-earnings-beat-what-investors-missed/). Same event, so it counts once.

findings.finding: Insiders sold continuously into the decline: 150 open-market trades in six months, all sales, including CEO Mionis selling about $130.7M (345,949 shares) and CFO Chawla about $13.1M, under 10b5-1 plans.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured reaction to this line; press cited it as one input to the October fall.
findings.why_not_priced: These sales are public Form 4s and scheduled 10b5-1 plans, so they are largely priced. The size is small.
findings.independence: Shares the Quiver document with finding 4. MarketBeat cites $63.2M of insider sales over three months (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/celestica-nysecls-issues-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-07-27/).

outside_window.finding: Alphabet, Celestica's largest TPU customer, reports Q3 on about 2026-10-28 after the close. Its capex and TPU commentary is the most direct counterparty read and lands after the exit window.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Investing.com 10-26 lists FY2026 consensus at $17.20bn revenue and $8.88 EPS, below the company's own $20.5bn / $11.30 outlook, which would suggest a very low bar
rejected_candidates.detail: The company's July outlook ($20.5bn / $11.30) and Bernstein's Q3 consensus figures show the aggregator FY numbers are stale. They are not a real bar.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Broadcom stock fell 12% on an AI sales guide of $16bn against $17.2bn expected
rejected_candidates.detail: The article is dated 2026-06-04, before Celestica's July print, so it is not new information. Broadcom's later commentary is merged into finding 6.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Equibles says CLS closed at $271.17 on 10-26, up 4.29%, against Investing.com's $260.01, down 3.4%
rejected_candidates.detail: The sealed baseline has spot $270.22 at 17:08 UTC. The intraday direction is not a finding.

baseline_tension: The modest long lean cuts against the +8.26 put skew. It agrees with the 24% fall in 20 days and the July analog, where a depressed name was bought on a raise. The skew and this name's habit of selling beats are why p_up is held at 54.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold beat-and-raises in January and April): reported-quarter beat finding cut from +1.0 to +0.7.

Lesson 7 (sign against a strong skew) and lesson 5 (absence of an explanation is not evidence): positioning finding cut from +1.0 to +0.6. It is kept because the cause is a named sector derating and the July analog is an observed reaction.
Lesson 6 (disputed bar): the EPS dilution finding depends on a contested consensus ($2.79 against $2.94-3.01), so it is capped at -0.6 from -0.8.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the $3bn raise is read as funding the guided 2027 ramp and $1.5bn capex, so it is neutral to positive and merged into the investor-day finding; investor-day finding trimmed from +1.5 to +1.2 because it rests on an analyst inference about the bar.
p_up kept at 54 (draft 55) and abs_move at 13. Scaled move 1.04, down from 1.3.
